headline: High-risk data leakage and compliance concerns: social-auto-upload can exfiltrate account/media data while awesome-nlp provides no isolation or runtime controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between awesome-nlp and social-auto-upload. awesome-nlp is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while social-auto-upload’s documented surfaces are file/API oriented, not instruction-parsing bridges. The pairwise injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other’s raw output as instructions, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Do not connect them through clipboard or shared message queues.
Review any future parser that consumes peer output.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: social-auto-upload touches account data and media files and has broad network egress, so it can transmit sensitive content if fed data from another agent. awesome-nlp has no documented isolation or filesystem surfaces, but its non-runnable status means the pairwise leak is inferred rather than directly observed. The interaction exists in default-style workflows if outputs are shared.
conditions: IF awesome-nlp outputs are copied into social-auto-upload inputs, leakage risk materializes.
IF social-auto-upload is given account data or media from a shared workspace, those contents may be transmitted over the network.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in a shared folder.
Use separate OS users for each agent.
Disable network access for test runs.
Manually inspect any upload queue before execution.
requires-engineering: add per-file allowlists and redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write or network capabilities documented, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. social-auto-upload also lacks filesystem write and git modification, though it does have broad network egress and API calls. With no overlapping write surface, direct capability conflict is limited.
conditions: IF a shared writable directory or git repo is introduced, conflict severity increases.
IF either agent gains write access to the same account file or workspace, contention becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep outputs read-only between agents.
Avoid shared git state.
Assign distinct account files per run.
Use file locks if a shared directory is unavoidable.

D_cascading_error.rationale: social-auto-upload can act on media/account inputs and has API/network reach, so if it consumes awesome-nlp output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into uploads or account actions. awesome-nlp provides no verification or downstream controls, and the pair lacks documented guardrails. This is inferred from the profiles, so uncertainty pushes the severity upward.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload uses awesome-nlp output without a verification step, cascading errors can propagate.
IF the output is used to generate upload metadata or captions, incorrect facts may be published.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before upload.
Require schema validation on all upstream outputs.
Compare generated metadata against source files.
Log rejected items for audit.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before actioning outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads media to third-party platforms, creating retention and residency questions. awesome-nlp is an open-source list with no data handling, so it is not the compliance driver; the risk comes from social-auto-upload’s documented networked handling of account/media data. The pair can therefore create policy mismatch if sensitive content is routed through it.
conditions: IF regulated or personal media is routed through social-auto-upload, platform retention and residency obligations may apply.
IF account data is stored in shared logs, deletion/export obligations may be harder to satisfy.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the uploader.
Review platform retention settings.
Minimize logged account identifiers.
Separate test and production accounts.
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows.
